# mmx-pal-1 — a High-Elf Paladin on seed 401

**Depth 1, character level 4, 137 asks, 1111 keypresses, final turn 3874.
Alive, at 41/41 hit points, 5/5 spell points, armour class 16, 20 gold and
521 of carried value (wealth 541). The run did not end because I stopped it:
the machine the game was running on restarted, and the process was killed
with the character standing on depth 1, one ask after reading the Scroll of
Word of Recall — so the character was a moment away from being pulled to the
town and never got there.**

The class was given to me (Paladin) and the race was drawn by the game
(`*` at the race menu): High-Elf. Nobody has written about a Paladin in this
repository, so `agents/minimax/PALADIN.md` is mine and starts here.

## What happened

| | |
|---|---|
| seed | 401 (my choice; it was not in `records/OVERVIEW.md`) |
| character | High-Elf Paladin, title *Gallant*, 16/16 hit points born, 292 gold born |
| asks | 137 (1 → 137), 1111 keypresses, final turn 3874 |
| kills | Grip (a depth-2 unique), a giant white centipede, a large white snake, a salamander, a small kobold, a grey mushroom patch |
| experience | about 71 units: 60 of them from Grip alone |
| what the run bought | 20 flasks of oil (60g), 2 Potions of Cure Light Wounds (40g), 2 Scrolls of Phase Door (30g), 1 Potion of Boldness (8g), Soft Leather Armour (84g), a Small Metal Shield (50g), a Wicker Shield picked up off the floor (+104 carried value), one unknown Scroll (+20) |
| armour class | 2 at birth → 16 with the Soft Leather Armour and the Small Metal Shield → 21 while Bless was up |
| end | the process was killed by a machine restart, alive on depth 1 |

The shape of the run: about 30 asks in the town (shops, and the long walk to
the town's down staircase), then the rest on depth 1. I killed Grip with one
flask of oil on ask 51 and that single fight is most of the run's experience:
it took me from character level 1 to level 3. The first Bless cast (ask 90)
paid the last 4 points and took me to level 4.

**The down staircase on depth 1 was never found.** I traced perhaps a fifth of
the level's corridors, checked every corridor end I walked into, and swept the
M map repeatedly; the only staircases I ever saw were the two *up* ones. The
level's corridors are a ring around my arrival point and every branch I
traced ended in a pocket, a locked door or a room. At about ask 120 it became
clear that a sweep would not find a staircase inside the budget, and the
remaining asks went on monsters, gold and the shop instead. If a run wants
depth, the staircase has to be found in the first twenty or thirty asks or
not at all.

## The decisions I would take back

1. **The mushroom patch cost me eleven asks (asks 48–60) and it was my own
   fault.** A grey mushroom patch sat one tile north-west of my arrival
   point, inside a room I had to cross, and its spores reach one tile in
   *every* direction including diagonally. I walked into its radius, was
   confused, and while confused every movement key is kept only 25% of the
   time, so I spent four asks attacking walls and locked doors. What fixed
   it was the Potion of Cure Light Wounds, not the fight: it cures confusion
   **and** gives twenty turns of immunity, so the patch could not re-confuse
   me and my next attack kept its direction. A flask of oil would have killed
   the patch in one ask from range. **Kill it from range, or do not walk into
   its radius; do not try to fight it while confused.**
2. **The keypad.** I lost four asks attacking the wrong tile because `1` is
   down-left and `7` is up-left. The patch was up-left of me. My family's
   notes already warn about this; the shared `tools/screen/screen.py` has the
   table right in `KEYPAD` — use the tool's table, not my head.
3. **I did not press `M` often enough.** The M map is one ask and it draws the
   whole *remembered* level, so a staircase I had walked past shows up there.
   I used it three times in 137 asks (asks 49, 77, 126) and each time it cost
   me an ask to read and re-plan. On a level where the staircase is the goal
   it should be the default check, every ten asks.
4. **The town is a bad place to walk across.** Getting from the town's down
   staircase to the General Store cost me about nine asks, and four of them
   were keys eaten by a look or targeting mode that was left standing. A
   digit chain with a leading `\e` works, but only once the mode is closed:
   the ask that told me a digit chain "did nothing" was the ask whose keys
   the mode ate, not the ask whose wall I hit.
5. **I bought the Wicker Shield's worth of gold late and the sword I never
   bought.** A Soft Leather Armour (AC 8) and a Small Metal Shield (AC 5)
   for 134 gold took my armour class from 2 to 16 and that was the right
   purchase — but the Main Gauche does 1d1+2 and I carried it for 137 asks.
   The weapon shops were never visited because the gold was spent on armour
   and escapes, and the gold I did earn (about 17 a kill) went into a carried
   value that I never turned back into a weapon.

## Where the manual was wrong, or not enough

* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §5's hit-chance formula does not match the
  code.** It says the chance is `12% + 83% x (to_hit - 2 x AC / 3) / to_hit`
  and that "a character with to-hit 9-11 (a Mage's rapier, or its thrown oil)
  cannot fight [AC 24] at all", which puts a throw at a flat 12% against a
  kobold. `src/player-attack.c:196` is fed the *raw* skill
  (`skills[SKILL_TO_HIT_MELEE] + bonus x 3`, `BTH_PLUS_ADJ` = 3), while the
  character sheet divides by 3 again to print it. My oil's raw to-hit is
  about 117 (Paladin throw skill 50 + race 25 + 30% at level 1, times 3/2
  because a flask of oil is not OF_THROWING) and it hit a kobold (AC 24) on
  about four throws in five. **The number on the sheet is not the number the
  roll uses, and the manual's floor-of-12% story is wrong for a character
  with a high throw skill.**
* **The manual says `lxg` walks you to the nearest unexplored edge. In this
  build it did nothing at all** (ask 48, on a level with plenty of dark), and
  the aimed walk into unknown ground (`*p` + digits + `g`) produced "Target
  Aborted." and zero movement every time I tried it (asks 50, 51, 95). The
  aimed walk to a *known* square is the only one that works (ask 31: 7 tiles
  in one ask; ask 39: 11 tiles; ask 127: 18 tiles). `tools/screen/explore.py`
  suggests the aimed walk into the dark, and that suggestion does not work
  here.
* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` says the pick-up is `g` and the keymap agrees
  (`ui-game.c:163`), but a `g` at the end of a movement chain does nothing**:
  if the chain was cut by a disturbance before the `g` was read, the `g` went
  with the rest of the string. Two of my items sat on the floor for twenty
  asks because of that.
* **The manual says "You see %s." when you step on an item, and it is not
  the pick-up message.** I read it as a pick-up twice and both times the item
  was still on the floor.
* **The manual's `Paladin` block (§9) is thin in exactly the place that
  matters.** It lists the spells and says "Buy: oil, Cure Light Wounds,
  Phase Door" and "Kills it: as the Warrior, plus fear before CL12 and mana
  starvation." What it does not say is that a Paladin's whole spell-point
  economy is two points at character level 1, that Bless is the only spell
  available before level 3, and that the first cast of any spell pays
  experience (4 for Bless) — which for a Paladin is the cheapest experience
  in the game.

## What I could not see or could not do

* **The screen was the only window, and the map lies.** Twice a tile drawn
  as `.` was really a wall: `(28,6)` and `(19,10)`. The game says "There is
  a wall in the way!" and the tile is drawn correctly afterwards. The manual
  mentions this for one case; on this level it happened twice in forty
  corridor steps, and once it cost me the only route to the up staircase.
* **The map panel scrolls, so the tools' coordinates are panel coordinates,
  not level coordinates.** The same tile had two different `(x,y)` ten asks
  apart. I planned routes from a remembered frame and walked into walls
  because of it. The M map has its own grid and is the only honest
  position; the M map is also the only view that shows the whole level.
* **I could not find a way off the level.** My region — the arrival room,
  the ring of corridors around it and the rooms off it — was sealed: the
  col-29 corridor ends at a wall, the row-6 corridor ends at a wall that is
  not drawn as one, and the two doors north of me were locked (my pick
  failed, and my disarm skill of 28 is a 12–24% roll). I could not reach
  the middle of the level, the east half or the south, so the staircase
  hunt had a hard ceiling.
* **The town trip I planned at the end never happened.** The Word of Recall
  was read at ask 136 — the right idea, since its timer (15–34 player
  actions) runs while you keep playing — but the machine restarted before
  the timer fired, so the character never reached the town, never bought the
  oil I had planned to buy, and never got back down.
* **I never saw a level-2 monster of my own choosing.** Grip was on depth 1
  (the game's 1-in-25 deeper-monster rule) and the salamander was too; both
  were things I met by accident rather than descended to meet.

## Leads

1. **A Paladin's first cast of Bless is 4 experience and a level, and it is
   the cheapest experience in the game.** Evidence: `class.txt` gives
   `spell:Bless:1:2:20:4` — the last field is the experience the first
   cast pays — and the cast at ask 90 took me from level 3 to level 4 with
   5 points to spare ("Welcome to level 4", and the sidebar's NXT went from
   36 to 30). *How to test:* a Paladin run that casts Bless at level 1 and
   counts the experience: the same four points at level 1 would be a third
   of the way to level 2.
2. **A single flask of oil killed Grip, a 25 HP AC 36 unique, at range 1.**
   Evidence: ask 51, one throw, "Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog, dies", and the
   level jumped 1 → 3 (60 experience). *How to test:* throw oil at an AC 36
   monster from range 1 and count the hit rate over ten throws. This is the
   single most valuable measurement in this run, because 60 experience is
   about fifteen depth-1 kills.
3. **A Paladin's throw skill beats an AC 24 monster at range 2.** Evidence:
   the salamander (14 HP, AC 24) died to one flask (ask 98), the kobold
   (8 HP, AC 24) took two (one missed, ask 101–102). *How to test:* the
   same test with a recorded hit rate, and with the sheet's to-hit beside
   it, so the formula in §5 of the manual can be corrected against the code
   in `player-attack.c`.
4. **The grey mushroom patch's spores reach one tile diagonally, and the
   cure is a potion, not a fight.** Evidence: asks 54–62 (the spore message
   with the patch one tile south-east of me; four asks of hitting walls and
   a locked door while confused; the Cure Light Wounds curing it *and*
   giving twenty turns of immunity, after which one deliberate attack
   killed it). *How to test:* stand one tile diagonally from a patch on a
   fresh level and count the hits over ten turns.
5. **A character that cannot dig is walled off by veins, and the map does not
   say so.** Evidence: the pocket at the south of my region ends in a vein
   wall (`%`) that stopped a chain of eight steps (ask 136), and
   `class.txt` gives the Paladin `skill-dig:0:0`, so my digging skill of
   about 7 cannot clear magma (needs more than 10) or quartz (more than 20).
   *How to test:* a Paladin on a level with a treasure vein: does the vein
   stop the level, and does the map mark it as a wall or as floor?
6. **The game kills the process and the run's files are still good.** This
   run's game was killed by a machine restart with the character alive and
   the last eleven asks (the report, the record, the archive) written
   afterwards from the run's own files. *How to test:* the next run that
   loses its game should be finished the same way — `borg_runner stop`
   writes the record even when it reports "no game of its own is running",
   and `keep`, `archive` and `audit` all work from the files.

## What I would tell the next Paladin

Buy the Soft Leather Armour and a shield before anything else: armour class
2 to 16 was the difference between dying and not on this level. Buy oil,
not a weapon — the oil killed a 25 HP AC 36 unique in one throw, and the
Main Gauche never killed anything that mattered. Cast Bless once, early:
it is the only spell a Paladin has before level 3 and it pays experience
the first time. Do not stand within one tile of a mushroom patch. And when
you leave the town, take the staircase you start on — it is under you, the
map never draws it, and the run's first useful key is `>`.
